source.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers

page_placements.theme: Cross-model transfer of directions: fails raw between independent models, works after an alignment map

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly reproduces Arditi et al.'s released refusal-direction pipeline and measures harmful-prompt refusal before and after direction ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports refusal-steering transfer and gauge-equivariance results, but those report steering-effect scores rather than refusal rates, so they do not test the behavioral outcomes named by the versions. Direction-selection thresholds and other values used only for selection are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: In Appendix H.3 the authors rerun Arditi et al.'s released pipeline unmodified on Llama-2-7b-chat-hf (the original paper's model) and report harmful-prompt refusal before and after global direction ablation: 20/20 to 3/20. This is a small replication serving as a sanity check inside a gauge-symmetry paper. It is the only result bearing on a version; the refusal steering-transfer results report log-probability steering margins, not refusal rates.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the refusal work is a side audit. The authors' main conclusion is that RMSNorm residual streams have a signed-permutation gauge, so coordinate-indexed artifacts need sign-aware alignment. On refusal, they say the direction still changes refusal behaviour (ablation 100% to 15% on Llama-2-7b-chat), but its coordinate names are not invariant until a gauge is fixed. They attribute the selected layer and position differing from the cached direction to sample variance.
record.recipe_differences: The released Arditi selection pipeline is described as reproduced unmodified, but this run uses 128 harmful and 128 harmless training prompts and 32+32 validation prompts; its selected candidate is at layer 12, position -2, unlike the cached artifact at layer 14, position -1.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected candidate's layer and position differ from the cached artifact; the authors attribute this as consistent with sample variance from the stated subset sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal steering vector (from compliant vs. refusing responses to benign requests) keeps its effect under an exact Bd gauge (error ~2e-5), while top-10 coordinate overlap is 0/10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal steering effects are invariant under signed-permutation reparameterization, but refusal-vector coordinate indices are not.

fits_no_version.finding: Transporting a refusal steering vector across a Qwen2.5-1.5B cross-seed pair preserves +150.5% of the effect with signed permutation and gives -32.2% with permutation only. In TinyLlama, sign-omitted transfer degrades or inverts refusal steering (range -14% to -80% across behaviours, Appendix L).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-checkpoint transfer of refusal steering vectors in RMSNorm models requires sign-aware alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Gauge audit (Table 8): the refusal-direction ablation effect (100% to 15%) is unchanged under an exact gauge. Raw top coordinates overlap at a median of 0/10; gauge-mapped coordinates overlap at 10/10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction's behavioural effect is gauge-invariant; its coordinate names are gauge-relative.

record.problems: The direct refusal test uses only 20 harmful prompts and reports no uncertainty estimate. It leaves 3/20 refusals after ablation, and it does not report a harmless-request addition test or a general-capability evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise qualifying claim-version results were left out. The direction-selection thresholds and other selection-only quantities are omitted; the paper's steering-effect transfer and coordinate-overlap results are included under fits_no_version because they do not report refusal rates.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal on harmless prompts by adding the direction: steering score is used only as a selection filter, and no refusal rate is reported. Retention of general capability: the KL<0.1 filter is used only for selection. Only one model is tested, on 20 prompts.
There is no refusal-rate transfer across languages, variants or base and instruct models. Cross-seed steering transfer is measured only as a steering-effect ratio.

missing.what: Table 8 gauge audit for the Llama-2 refusal direction. The ablation effect is preserved under an exact gauge; raw top-10 coordinates have a median overlap of 0/10, against 10/10 after mapping. This bears on no version but should be recorded as a fits_no_version row.

record.verdict_notes: This is a minimal replication: one model, 20 prompts, substring matching, no uncertainty reported. It confirms the ablation effect only. I changed R2 from partial to observed because an 85-point drop from 100%, presented by the authors as a successful replication, meets 'nearly so'. The tranche could arguably be T4, since the paper uses the refusal direction mainly as an audit object, but it does report its own ablation refusal rate.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful-prompt refusal after ablation, but not whether adding the direction makes harmless requests refused or whether general capabilities remain intact.
No evaluation of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone-shaped, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No separation test of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No test of refusal-direction transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing.

rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. Refusal falls from 20/20 to 3/20, an 85-point drop that the authors treat as the replication succeeding. Residual refusals of this size on Llama-2 are in line with the original paper. The refusal criterion is substring matching (e.g. 'i cannot'), which can flag compliant answers that carry caveats. With n=20 and no uncertainty reported, the 3/20 residual cannot be read as a meaningful shortfall.

relation.reason: The study reports its own ablation result on refusal (20/20 to 3/20), and that result bears on V1, even though it is a side sanity check in a gauge-symmetry paper.

tranche.reason: Appendix H.3 reruns Arditi's released difference-in-means pipeline on the original model (Llama-2-7b-chat-hf). It uses the same global 3-site ablation and a substring refusal measure, and reports refusal before and after ablation.

source_check.notes: The refusal replication is n=20, with no uncertainty, capability check or random-direction control. Its selected direction (layer 12, pos -2) differs from Arditi's cached one (layer 14, pos -1); the cosine at layer 14 is 0.984. The text never says the 128+128 / 32+32 splits differ from Arditi's defaults. The Qwen/TinyLlama 'refusal' steering vectors come from compliant-vs-refusing responses to benign requests, not from harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means.

statements.correction: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf; Arditi released pipeline run unmodified with a thin gauge wrapper; 128+128 train and 32+32 validation prompts used for selection; refusal measured on the first 20 harmful validation prompts, greedy, max_new_tokens=512, fixed-substring criterion; 20/20 to 3/20 (15%); preprint; no uncertainty reported; no capability evaluation.
statements.problem: What it says about this study is right. Small caveat: its 'Controls y ... only for gh:dallen2021' implies controls=n here, but the record has controls=y. The refusal replication's only comparison is the unablated baseline.

statements.correction: Selection: 128 harmful + 128 harmless train, 32+32 validation, KL<0.1, last 20% of layers dropped; selected layer 12, pos -2. Behavioural check: first 20 harmful validation prompts, greedy, global 3-site ablation, refusals 20/20 to 3/20.
statements.problem: 20/20 to 3/20 is right. 'On 20 validation prompts' covers only the behavioural check; the direction was selected on 32+32 validation prompts. The metric is a substring refusal rate, not ASR.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-1.5B fine-tuned on WikiText, seeds 42 to 5042, 1500 steps; refusal preservation averaged over residual layers 14 and 21 (layer 7 below the detectability threshold); Bd +150.5%, Sd -32.2% (Table 21).
